اتخذوا أيمانهم جنة (ittakhadhu aymanahum junnah, "They have taken their oaths as a shield"): i.e., a cover behind which they concealed their wealth and secured their blood.

فصدوا عن سبيل الله (fasaddu ʿan sabil Allah, "and so they barred [others] from the way of Allah"): i.e., they barred thereby from the way of Allah, that is, from jihad against them.

إنهم ساء ما كانوا يعملون (innahum sa'a ma kanu ya'malun, "Indeed, evil is what they used to do"): i.e., evil is what they were doing of hypocrisy.

ذلك (dhalika, "That"): i.e., the evil of their conduct.

بأنهم آمنوا ثم كفروا (bi'annahum amanu thumma kafaru, "because they believed and then disbelieved"): i.e., they believed with their tongues, then disbelieved in their hearts, that is, they persisted in that state.

فطبع على قلوبهم (fatubi'a ʿala qulubihim, "so their hearts were sealed"): i.e., they were sealed with disbelief.

فهم لا يفقهون (fahum la yafqahun, "so they do not understand"): i.e., faith; they do not know its meaning or its soundness.

تعجبك أجسامهم (tu'jibuka ajsamuhum, "their bodies impress you"): i.e., because of their beauty, for Ibn Ubayy was a large, healthy, handsome man of eloquent tongue.

وإن يقولوا تسمع لقولهم (wa in yaqulu tasma' liqawlihim, "and if they speak, you listen to their speech"): i.e., because of their eloquence and fluency of tongue.

كأنهم خشب مسندة (ka'annahum khushubun musannadah, "as if they were propped-up pieces of wood"): i.e., as if, because of the bulk of their bodies and their neglect of reflection and lack of understanding, they were propped-up timber: forms without spirits, bodies without minds.

يحسبون كل صيحة عليهم (yahsabuna kulla sayhatin ʿalayhim, "they think every shout is against them"): i.e., they suppose that every loud sound they hear, such as a call in an army camp or the announcing of a lost animal, is aimed at them, because of the terror in their hearts lest there descend something that would make their blood lawful to shed.

هم العدو فاحذرهم (hum al-ʿaduwwu fahdharhum, "They are the enemy, so beware of them"): i.e., the utter enemy, so beware lest they spread your secrets or intend you harm.

قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون (qatalahumu Allah anna yu'fakun, "May Allah curse them! How are they turned away?"): i.e., may Allah curse them; how are they turned away from faith while they witness its lights and proofs?

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Most High, ﴿When the hypocrites come to you﴾: the occasion of revelation of this surah is that Zayd ibn Arqam (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I was with my uncle, and I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul say: 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse,' and he said: 'If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.' So I mentioned that to my uncle, and he mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger sent for Ibn Ubayy and his companions, and they swore that they had not said it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed them and called me a liar, and I was struck with a grief such as I had never experienced, so I sat in my house. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'When the hypocrites come to you' up to 'the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it.' So he sent for me and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it, then said: 'Indeed Allah has confirmed you.'"

By their false oaths that they are believers, they protected themselves, their wives and their offspring from killing and captivity, and thereby they barred themselves from the way of Allah, and barred others who follow them, and barred the believers from fighting them, by the outward false faith they displayed.

The Most High said: ﴿Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾: He, exalted is He, censures their state and denounces their conduct, which is taking their oaths as a shield and barring from the way of Allah. And His words, the verse numbered [3]: ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed﴾: i.e., the evil of their conduct and the ugliness of their behavior result from their having believed and then doubted or wavered, so they became hypocrites. There also followed from this the sealing of their hearts, so they do not understand the meaning of faith nor distinguish its soundness from its falsehood. This is the condition of one who goes deep into disbelief: a seal is placed upon his heart, so faith finds no path to a heart locked with the seal of disbelief and the stamp of hypocrisy, doubt and polytheism.

His words in verse [4]: ﴿And when you see them, their bodies impress you﴾: i.e., when you see them, O our Messenger, and look at them, their bodies impress you because of their beauty, for Ibn Ubayy was a large and handsome man, "and if they speak, you listen to their speech," because of their eloquence and fluency of tongue. His words, ﴿as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾, are a striking simile: because of the length and beauty of their bodies, their lack of understanding and their scarcity of good, they are like propped-up timber against a wall, that neither intercedes nor benefits, as the saying goes.

His words, ﴿They think every shout is against them﴾: this is because of their fear and the terror that has taken hold of their souls, as a result of the disbelief, enmity and hatred for Islam and its people that they conceal. So whenever they hear a shout in a camp or the voice of one announcing a lost animal, they expect that they are meant by it, like the case of the traitor. What they fear most is that the Qur'an will descend to expose them and tear away their veils. The Most High said: ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them, O our Messenger, for their hearts are with your enemies, and they await misfortune for you.﴾

The Most High said: ﴿May Allah curse them! How are they turned away?﴾: He has recorded upon them a curse that will not leave them until the Day of Resurrection. How are they turned away from the truth, while its lights envelop them, the Qur'an descends, the Messenger teaches and purifies, and the effects of that are evident in the believers in their opinions and morals? They witness none of that, and we seek refuge in Allah from the blindness of hearts and the obliteration of insight.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification that a lie is whatever contradicts belief, even if it matches the reality.

2- A warning against persisting in sin, for it necessitates the sealing of the heart and deprives its owner of guidance.

3- A warning against being deceived by outward appearances, such as fine dress and eloquence of tongue.

4- Disclosure of the psychology of the traitor, the oppressor and the criminal: fear, and dread of every sound or word, lest it be a declaration of their condition and an exposure of their crimes.

﴿ورأيتهم يصدون﴾: i.e., they turn away from what they were called to, while being arrogant.

﴿لن يغفر الله لهم﴾: i.e., despair of Allah's forgiveness for them.

﴿إن الله لا يهدي القوم الفاسقين﴾: i.e., because it is Allah's way that He does not guide the people who are deeply immersed in defiance of the obedience of the Lord, the Exalted, and who remain so.

﴿يقولون﴾: i.e., to the people of Madinah.

﴿لا تنفقوا على من عند رسول الله﴾: i.e., the Emigrants (muhajirun).

﴿حتى ينفضوا﴾: i.e., disperse from him.

﴿لئن رجعنا إلى المدينة﴾: i.e., from a military campaign they were on, which was the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq.

The noble context continues to speak of the hypocrites. This was when Ibn Ubayy uttered the wicked words he said, among them his saying about the Emigrants: "Fatten your dog and it will devour you." And his saying to his companions: "Do not spend on the Emigrants until they disperse from Muhammad (ﷺ)." And his saying, threatening: "If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner." By "the mightier" he meant himself and his fellow hypocrites, and by "the meaner" the Ansar and the Emigrants. When he had said all this, most of it during the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of it. He came and swore by Allah that he had said none of that at all, and he went away. Then this noble surah was revealed to refute him.

Allah said to His Messenger: ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them⦆, so He made His Messenger despair of their forgiveness. Ibn Ubayy was among the most defiant of the defiant, for he combined lying, false swearing, hypocrisy, enmity, hostility, arrogance and inward disbelief. 3- All sources of provision are in the hand of Allah, the Exalted; so provision should be sought through obedience to Allah and His Messenger, not through disobeying them.

4- True might belongs to Allah, to His Messenger and to the believers; therefore the believer must not abase himself or demean himself before a disbeliever.

﴿حتى ينفضوا﴾: i.e., disperse from him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 63, verse 9–11:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you﴾: i.e., do not preoccupy you.

﴿From the remembrance of Allah﴾: such as prayer, Hajj, recitation of the Qur'an, and remembrance of Allah by the heart and the tongue.

﴿And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾: i.e., whoever is diverted by his wealth and children from performing the obligations, so that he abandons prayer, Hajj, or other obligations, has lost the reward of the Hereafter.

﴿And spend from what Allah has provided for you﴾: i.e., the obligatory expenditure, such as zakat, and expenditure in jihad, as well as the recommended kind.

﴿Why did You not delay me﴾: i.e., "Why not delay me?" He asks for a postponement, and it is not accepted from him.

﴿So I would give charity and be among the righteous﴾: i.e., so that I may pay zakat, perform Hajj, and increase in voluntary acts and righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O you who have believed﴾: He, the Exalted, addressed the believers to advise them that their state should not be like the state of the hypocrites whose discipline was mentioned earlier in the context. So He said to them: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿do not let your wealth or your children divert you﴾, i.e., do not preoccupy you from the remembrance of Allah by performing His obligations, avoiding what He has forbidden, increasing in obedience to Him, and drawing near to Him by various acts of devotion. Then He warned them, advising them, saying: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., whoever is diverted by his wealth and children from the worship of Allah, ﴿those are the losers﴾, the distant ones, who will lose on the Day of Resurrection by being deprived of Paradise and its bliss and by being in the abode of punishment, having neither family nor children there. The Mighty and Majestic went further in guiding them, saying: ﴿And spend from what We have provided you﴾, hastening before the term, for you do not know when you will die, ﴿before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, why did You not delay me for a short term so I would give charity and be among the righteous?"﴾ He says this wishing, seeking, and urging in his request: "My Lord," i.e., O Lord, "why did You not delay me to a near term," i.e., to a time close to this, "so I would give charity with my wealth, and be among the righteous, so I would perform Hajj and draw near to You, O Lord, by what You love of various kinds of devotion and acts of obedience." But his wishing, his request, and his supplication will not benefit him, because it is the eternal decree of Allah that He, the Exalted, will never delay a soul when its term has come, i.e., when the time of its death has arrived. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ urges the believers to reform their deeds and to prepare provision for their Hereafter, by informing them that He is aware of their deeds and well-acquainted with them.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The prohibition of being preoccupied with wealth and children while neglecting some obligations and duties.

2- The prohibition of delaying Hajj while able to perform it, procrastinating and dragging one's feet, despite believing in its obligation.

3- The obligation of zakat, and encouragement toward specific charities such as charity for jihad, and general charity to the poor and needy.

4- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense.
